propositions: Tool-result message history is re-sent uncached on every agentic turn, causing input cost to grow quadratically (O(N^2)) with turn count while only two of four available cache breakpoints are enabled.

The agentic path applies only anthropic_cache_instructions and anthropic_cache_tool_definitions, but omits anthropic_cache and anthropic_cache_messages despite both existing in pydantic-ai 1.107.1, leaving the growing message tail unbilled to cache.

Cache telemetry is invisible to monitoring because warn_if_cache_ineffective gate fires only when cache_read_tokens == 0, but the system block hits cache so the predicate never triggers despite massive uncached message overhead.

Anthropic and Bedrock providers require different cache configuration keys (anthropic_cache vs bedrock_cache_messages); Bedrock rejects top-level cache_control as invalid, creating an asymmetry that must be handled separately per provider.
Multi-turn agentic runs accumulate ~2.6k token tool results per turn, and without message-tail caching a 40-turn review re-sends ~80k tokens uncached at turn 40 that were already sent at turn 39.
Single-turn non-agentic paths must remain byte-identical after changes to avoid regression, requiring conditional cache configuration based on execution mode.
